appraisal_events.evidence: Aimé appartenait à une race plus ancienne que celle du prince, donc plus noble. [...] Aimé, dessalé par la vie d'hôtel, où il avait conquis, du reste, un rang éminent...
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator describes Aimé, a senior hotel maître d'hôtel, as belonging to an older and nobler lineage than the prince he serves and as having attained an eminent rank through his career, marking a local elevation of his professional standing.

appraisal_events.evidence: Je refusai nettement... « C'est bon, nous ne viendrons pas », me dit-elle d'une voix tremblante de colère. [...] un sourire qui ne lui appartenait pas en propre... sauf quelques-uns très raffinés, comme Swann ou comme Charlus.
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator firmly rebuffs Mme Verdurin's controlling insistence on joining his outing with Albertine; her forced, borrowed hostess smile and furious, petty reaction when refused expose her as unrefined and controlling, in contrast to the narrator's cited standard of the truly refined.

appraisal_events.evidence: cette expression, que Odette employait au temps où elle cherchait elle aussi à se faire son petit clan et à attirer les clients en ne bougeant pas, dût-elle souvent ne pas faire ses frais, et qu'elle traduisait avec contresens en « par principe »
appraisal_events.explanation: In a brief aside, the narrator mocks Odette's earlier attempts to build her own salon in imitation of Mme Verdurin, noting these efforts often failed and that she also misused the idiom, marking her as socially and linguistically inferior.

status_effects.explanation: Aimé is locally elevated by the narrator's admiring account of his lineage, seriousness, and eminent rank among hotel staff.
Mme Verdurin is diminished by her exposed manipulative insistence, insincere hostess smile, and childish fury when the narrator refuses her offer.
By successfully resisting Mme Verdurin's intrusive offer despite her anger, the narrator preserves his desired private time with Albertine, gaining emotional leverage in the encounter.
Odette is mildly diminished by the narrator's ironic aside about her past unsuccessful attempts at hosting and her malapropism.
